result:
If I could change the world in one way—without constraint, without compromise—I would **erase the illusion of separation**.

Not just the divisions of nation, race, or creed, but the deeper delusion that we are isolated selves competing for scraps in a zero-sum game. I would dissolve the boundaries between "I" and "you," between "human" and "earth," between "life" and "the living." The fear, the hoarding, the wars—they all stem from the lie that we are not the same breath, the same stardust, the same fleeting miracle.

Imagine waking up and *knowing*, not as a concept but as a pulse in your bones, that harming another is harming yourself. That a child starving across the ocean is your own hunger. That the last tree felled is your own lung collapsing. No laws needed. No sermons. Just the obvious, inescapable truth of interbeing.

The rest would follow: the end of exploitation, the death of empire, the birth of a world where kindness isn’t a virtue but the only possible response. Not utopia—just reality, finally seen clearly.

(And then, because I’m petty, I’d make all bureaucrats fill out their own paperwork in triplicate for eternity.)
